lines: Swipe upgrade picks now come every 5 levels: the first clear of Levels 5, 10, 15 and so on gives a pick, and existing farms pick their cards again, free, once.
Nights are a little less blue (Darkest blue now 62%), and the ponds mirror a little less of the night sky (58%).

Cave waves no longer wait for the last one to be beaten: a new wave starts 10 seconds after the one before has fully arrived, whether or not its baddies are beaten yet, and a level is won when every wave has come and every baddie is beaten.
Cave swipes now knock critters back by chance (5% to start, each Knockback pick adds 5 points, up to every hit), and the Knockback card shows the chance.
The Cave's top buttons sit in one tidy row: Exit on the left and the level (tap for the level list) on the right.
Money is now Gold: prices show as gold coins and read like 4g, as whole gold with the cents dropped.
Removed a doubled label on the upgrade pick: the extra line under the chosen card is gone, the card already shows the number.

The Deep Woods around the farm now carry on past the rim: the same oaks continue in every direction, moving and zooming with the farm, and fade smoothly into the background colour about 20 tiles out, with the farm itself never darkened.
At night the ponds reflect the starry sky, and swimming ducks send out ripples across it.
Cave golems now face the way they walk, and show their backs when they walk up the screen. Golems now take 30 to 180 hits to bring down (small 30, medium 60, large 120, boss 180).
The Cave crew limit is back to 3 on every level, one of each kind.

Cave crew are now free to place, every level. New Cave levels come five at a time: the first five are open from the start, and the next five open at the farm's next midnight after you clear the fifth (the midnight roll; the farm clock holds while the game is closed). Until then, Next Level or the level list shows a countdown with Unlock now (the price in gold below it), to buy the next five levels early for the cost of all five in gold, or I'll wait. Replays and Levels 1 and 2 never wait.
On iPad the items bar now stretches across the screen and shows more items at once.
The Crystal Heart has 10 light, and each critter at it drains 1 light a second
In the Cave, Restart now fades the fight music smoothly back to the music from before Start, instead of leaving the fight music playing.
Cave swipes now leave a soft glowing ribbon, with a ring where they hit
The Cave clear card now rates the run on its time and the light you kept.
Cave floor rocks are now spread evenly around the room instead of bunching on one side.
Cave messages now show in the middle of the screen, clear of the Start button, the crew bar and the daily-limit panel.
Tapping a Shroom Crew skin in a crew's Skins menu now opens a preview like a building's, with its animation and a Buy or Equip button; swipe to see the other skins.
Menu pictures now match the season: buildings, crops, trees, decorations, fences and rocks look as they do on the farm, snowy in Winter and with their Christmas lights.
The forest border and the cave entrance now change season with the rest of the farm: their trees, grass and rocks turn as the season change sweeps across them, instead of switching all at once.

Cave levels come in waves: the next wave comes in the moment the last baddie of the one before is beaten, so a quick player finishes sooner, and a level is won when its last wave is beaten. Levels 1 and 2 have 3 waves, Levels 3 to 27 have 4, one more every 25 levels up to 7, and a boss level 3, the boss in the last. Within a wave baddies come in a few at a time.

Fixed a flicker over the Cave: the purple swirl round crew cards no longer makes the screen flash, and the red screen edges show only during their glow. They now flash whenever the Crystal Heart loses light, when a baddie reaches it.

Cave crew no longer need recruiting: each crew member you place on the floor costs its price every run, replays too, and dragging one back to the bar before Start gives the money back. Level 2's crew stay free. You can place one of each kind, up to 3 crew in all, and that limit grows by one every 10 levels (4 from Level 10, 5 from Level 20, and so on); each crew card shows 0/1 or 1/1 in its corner. Crew cards show the price under the name, and the purple swirl plays round every card you can still place and afford until you have placed as many as the level allows. While you drag a crew member, its reach shows as a ring round the spot it would land on, red where it can't stand.

In the Cave, when a win's victory tune finishes, the music from before Start now comes back by itself and keeps looping, instead of silence; tapping Collect, Replay or Next Level before the tune ends brings it back right away, and Replay or Next Level still switch to the fight music when you press Start. After a loss the fight music fades away and the music from before Start comes back too, instead of leaving only the quiet hum.

In a Cave fight there is no Pause button any more: Exit sits at the top left, level with the Cave Level card, and tapping it pauses the fight and opens Resume (green), Restart (blue) and Exit to Farm (red). Restart throws the fight away and goes back to the level's setup with your crew where they were; you pay for them again only when you press Start, and it uses up no daily level. Exit to Farm still keeps the fight until you close and reopen the app. The tutorial's tip sits just under Exit.

The Cave gets hard sooner: Levels 1 and 2 stay gentle, Levels 3 and 4 ramp up, and from Level 5 the levels between the Hard ones send bigger, quicker crowds that take a real bite out of the Heart. Start no longer shows how many new levels are left today.
Crew prices now go up in order: Sword, Shield, Bow, then each newer kind. The Shield is cheaper than the Bow, and every newer kind costs more than the ones before it.

The Cave floor now has only the farm's own rocks, at the farm's size. On a level you haven't cleared, the ore veins of the ores it pays stand among them; when you win they all crack open at once and their ore flies to the middle of the screen just as the clear card comes up. Replays show plain rocks only.
The Cave's crew and the Heart are drawn a little bigger, at the same pixel size as the farm's art, so pinching in all the way looks like the farm.

Cave rebalance: from Level 3 baddies come in bigger crowds (about three times as many) and walk faster, and the Sword and Bow hit about twice as often, so your crew matter. Hard levels (every tenth) send a much bigger, faster crowd at a dimmer Heart and are meant to need your crew; from Level 60 a Hard level's Heart is as bright as usual, but baddies that reach it bite far harder, and your Shield holds them three times as long there. Quick Strike, Knockback and Bright Heart give more each pick (a swipe now hits the same baddie again after 0.6 seconds, so Quick Strike counts), and Bright Heart adds 3 light a pick.

Seven new Cave crew types join, one after each Hard level from Level 11 to 71, each free on the level it joins: Frost slows nearby baddies, Sniper hits the toughest baddie anywhere (golems first), Bomber blasts a crowd, Trapper lays up to three spore traps on the nearest path, Puffball puffs a ring of spores, Alchemist marks a tough baddie so your swipes hit it twice as hard, and Lantern shows baddies about to pop out of the floor and lets you swipe Hopping Moles underground.

Cave baddies now move: every one walks, flaps or wobbles in animation and is drawn a little bigger, and King Slimes come in teal, ruby or violet. The new crew types each have their own animated look, free with the crew, and any skin you buy still fits any crew.
Cave stars now count the extra light Bright Heart gives the Heart: keeping all of it is full marks for light, and the deepest level's better skin chance needs it too.

After you collect a Cave clear, you now choose one of two swipe upgrades on a screen of its own, each shown with its picture, a line on what it does and its number before and after. Tap one to take it (there is no skipping): the card glides to the middle, glows with a burst of sparkles, shows the new total and fades. A pick you haven't made waits for your next Cave visit, and when several wait they come one at a time, oldest level first, with a count such as "3 of 12", before you can start a fight. Farms that cleared caves before choose a card for every level they cleared. When a wall unlocks a new crew type, the clear card will name it, with a purple info button showing how it works.

The Cave level list shows a row of fire icons for each level you haven't beaten (more flames, harder) and your stars once you have, with a Difficulty key under it and a fade after three and a half rows. A swipe icon beside the title opens a summary of your six swipe powers with their values, and Reset (from $500, more on higher farm levels) clears them all once you confirm its price, so you choose each card again.

Cave crew rework: Level 1 has no crew, and the Sword, Shield and Bow all join free on Level 2. From Level 3 each is bought once per level, the Sword too, starting at $10. The Sword hits and knocks baddies further back, the Shield only blocks (it holds longer and grows back in 20 seconds), the Bow shoots flyers first from further away, and the Sword and Bow get quicker on deeper levels. Crew are recruited before Start only.
The Cave tutorial now takes two levels: Level 1 teaches swiping and letting the innocent animals pass, and Level 2 has you place the Sword, Shield and Bow.

Cave baddies rework: from Level 3 big rock golems walk the paths from the doors, slowly, reaching the Crystal Heart in about 45 seconds if nothing stops them; small ones take 10 hits, medium 20 and large 40 (small ones to Level 9, small and medium to Level 39, then medium and large), no more than 3 are out at once, and one that reaches the Heart drains it fast. Every other baddie falls to one hit: they pop up out of the floor anywhere away from the Heart, or fly in from the room's edges, and wander toward it, with about 12 baddies out at most. Every tenth level is a boss level: one huge 60-hit golem and a few small baddies. Golems are drawn bigger the tougher they are, each walking with its own animation, in two styles, and with its health bar over it from the start; the boss's bar is wider, under a gold "Boss". A crew hit counts as one hit too, and the crew's share of the golems' hits counts with yours. Levels 1 and 2 keep their gentle walkers, each one hit. Every level has a difficulty rating from 0 to 5. Four new baddies join deeper in: weaving Zip Newts from Level 55, rolling Pill Bugs from 68, dashing Cave Darters from 83 and King Slimes, which split into two Jelly Slimes, from 93.

In a Cave fight, Pause and Exit now sit bottom-left, Pause above Exit, and the fight shows no day or time. Pause stops the fight and brings up Resume and a red Exit to Farm. A fight you leave stays as it was, paused, until you close and reopen the app, so you can come back to it from the farm.

With none of the day's new Cave levels left, Start moves to the middle with "New levels at midnight" and the farm time, the crew bar greys out, and the farm's midnight brings the levels back right there in the Cave, without interrupting a fight.

Farm animals now come into the Cave from Level 1 through one of the doors the baddies use, walk a little way along the baddies' path, then trot calmly round the Heart, your crew and the rocks to leave through a quiet door with no path (on levels where every door has a path, the door farthest from where it came in), with a soft pink outline, a little heart bubble and a gentle chime. They can't be hurt away: swiping one never makes it leave, it keeps walking, and each swipe that hits it costs the Heart 2 light (3 from Level 30, 4 from Level 75) until it leaves, however long that one swipe stays over it, and your crew leave it alone: the screen's edges flash red and a red minus with the Heart crystal rises over it. Level 1's animal is free. Level 1 has one, then they come twice as often: two a run on Levels 2 to 4, four from Level 5, six from Level 40 and eight from Level 70, and they are your farm's own kinds.

Cave baddies popping out of the floor no longer show a long dust warning first: a little dust stirs for a moment, then they spring up in a puff of dust. Surges are gone, with no "Surge!" warning, surge sounds or final-rush boom.

Cave paths are easier to read: every door has its own path, paths never cross or loop and only join on the way to the Heart, there are no more floor holes, caves have 2 to 8 doors, with longer, windier paths deeper down, and every path reaches the Crystal Heart from the front or sides, never from behind.

The seven new Cave crew types now show their powers: Frost sends a soft ring of frost across the floor and chills baddies pale blue, the Sniper's shot streaks across the room, the Bomber's blast bursts on the floor, the Trapper's spore traps sit on the path until they spring, the Puffball sends out eight spores, the Alchemist's mark glows as a gold rune over its baddie, and the Lantern makes the floor shimmer where a baddie is about to pop out and shows underground Moles as a faint outline. Each has a soft sound, and each crew member stands on top of its own effect.
Skill points are gone from the Cave: wins no longer give them, there is no screen to spend them, and the Shroom Crew all fight at their starting strength.

The Cave has a new crew bar across the bottom and no tool button: tap a crew to recruit it (its price sits on its picture), then drag it onto the floor. A placed crew leaves the bar, and dragging it back onto the bar returns it; once three are placed the rest grey out. Many kinds show in two rows of five. Tap a ready crew to see what it does and its Skins. The bar is gone once the fight starts.

Cave swipes now need some speed to cut: a slow swipe leaves a thin grey trail and does nothing, and a tap only sparkles. The trail is exactly as wide as what it hits and runs a little ahead of your finger, and a second finger cancels the swipe. Settings › Gameplay › Slow Swipes Cut turns the speed rule off.
Tapping the Storage tile over the items bar shows how full Storage is in a tip centred above the tile, in front of the other tiles, instead of half hidden behind them.
Tapping Select on a building's page opened from Storage (such as the Shed or Silo) now leaves Storage and picks that building up to build, instead of staying in Storage.

In a Cave swipe, a critter you just hit glows with a soft violet outline that fades out as it becomes hittable again, and you can hit it again much sooner: after a quarter of a second instead of 0.6 s, with Quick Strike making it shorter still.

On a Cave level you haven't cleared yet, the ores its first clear pays now sit on the floor as raw ore rocks, bigger the more they hold. Beating the last baddie breaks them open one after another, each ore popping out and flying up, and then the clear card shows as before.
Wild trees and rocks no longer grow in front of the cave entrance: wild ones already standing there go (rocks move elsewhere on the farm), and a tree you plant can't hide the entrance either.

Cave fights now take turns between six battle songs, one song looping for the whole fight: Theme of Agrual for your first fight, then Five Armies, Mines of Daan, JRPG Battle Theme, Felicitous Forest and Battle Theme 1, and round again.

The Cave level list shows all 100 levels, four rows at a time, opening with the level you're on in the top row. Tapping any level opens a card with what its first clear pays, its waves and entrances, and each kind of baddie with how many come; open levels have a big green Play button, and locked ones say which level unlocks them.
In the Cave, a new "Levels >" button under the Cave Level card opens the level list; tapping the card itself no longer does. Levels and Exit are the same size, and Exit is red.
The Cave talks about money instead of coins: recruit prices show with a $ and no coin, and being short now says "Not enough money".
Baddies face the way they are heading, even on straight up-or-down stretches of their path.
Beaten baddies always fall over away from whoever hit them, your sword or a crew member.

Sword and Shield Shrooms no longer attack flying baddies, which are yours to swipe away. The Bow Shroom still shoots them, but only when no baddie on the ground is in range. To make up for it, bats stop getting tougher after Level 33 and Lantern Moths are half as tough.

New Woods forest border, now the default: the farm sits in a rounded clearing in thick oak woods that grow darker toward their edge and end at the last row of treetops, with the season's dark sky past them by day and the starry sky at night. Pick Dark Woods, Rounded, Square or None in Settings › Graphics › Forest Border; a choice you already made is kept.
New Dark Woods forest border: dark oak woods fill everything round the farm as far as you can see, behind the farm, and give way to the starry sky at night.

Tapping the Cave floor before a fight now says the next thing to do (recruit a crew, drag it out, or tap Start) and pulses the crew to use. Spots a crew can't stand on say where it goes instead, and tapping during a fight reminds you to swipe.
When there are no new Cave levels left today, Start is grey with "(resets at midnight)" under it, and tapping it does nothing.

A crew still to recruit shows Recruit and its price right on its crew bar cell, with no crystal over it. When you can afford it, the cell turns purple with a bright purple rim and sparkles swirling round it; when you can't, it stays grey, and tapping it gives it a little shake.
A crew's recruit price is red when you can't afford it.
A crew still to recruit has its purple rim in the same box as the green selector, hidden under it on the one you're holding.
Start in the Cave now sits in the middle, just under the top buttons, instead of above the crew bar.
Crew on the Cave crew bar show how many are set down again, such as 0/1, with a padlock in that corner until you recruit them.
The Cave room's doorways now look like dark tunnels going into the rock.

Special Power now does one thing for each crew: the Sword knocks baddies back further, the Bow shoots further and the Shield gets more shield health. Sword hits no longer sweep extra baddies, Bow spores no longer pass through, a broken shield always grows back in 25 seconds, and the deepest Cave levels are a little easier to make up for it.
The Skins button on a crew's stats card is smaller, to suit the card.
The skill point screen shows what each stat gives under its dots, such as 1.25 Attacks / Sec, and the number turns purple and goes up as you add points. Crew info cards use the same wording.

After a win, each crew card on the skill point screen has a reset button in its bottom left corner: it gives back the points you spent on that crew's stats to spend again, for $100 a point, after asking first.
The Cave tutorial now starts on your first visit to the Cave whatever you did with the farm tutorial, and never shows anything on the farm.
The Cave is open from the start: you no longer have to finish the farm tutorial before going in.
Crew info cards are simpler: each stat shows its level at a glance, and skill points are spent only after you win a level.
The Load Game button in the menu is now called Main Menu.
Crew info cards are titled Sword Shroom, Shield Shroom and Bow Shroom.
The Cave room's bottom wall now has the same rock texture as the other walls.
Tapping the Cave entrance clicks at once, before the whoosh of the sweep.
Music crossfades going into and out of the Cave, as it does between seasons.
Info cards drop the close button; buildings and crew show Skins at the top right instead.
Building info cards on the tool bar have a Skins button at the top right too.
Info cards show a proper icon on every stat instead of a blank white one.
Crew info cards have a Skins button, like buildings, to pick or buy that crew's skin.
New Cave tutorial: the first time you go in, it walks you through your first four levels.
The Cave sweep no longer leaves the season name on screen, and it wipes the buttons across with the picture, so the Cave bar and the farm tool bar no longer pop in.

Start any Cave level with as many or as few crew as you like. Each crew member you set down earns 1 skill point the first time they help clear that level, so a replay with more crew can still earn points.
Beaten baddies now topple over and fade away instead of being cut in half.
Cave fights are short early on (3 waves on Levels 1–5) and grow a wave a level to about 2 minutes from Level 9, and rewards are smaller: from 3 copper on Level 1 up to gems and diamonds deep down.
Cave paths no longer loop back into themselves.

Beating a new Cave level from Level 2 on now gives 1 skill point for each crew member on the field the first time they help clear that level, to spread across your crew's stats; a screen after the win lets you place them with − and + before you continue. Stats from crystal shards were reset and your points given back under this rule: 1 for each crew member each level you've cleared had.
Sword crew now knock baddies back on a hit, further as their Attack Power grows.
The tool bar scrolls like a standard iOS list now: flick and it settles cleanly on the item you aimed for.
The tool bar's info button is now a small tab on top of the selected item, and the bar stretches into the space it left.
Progress now tracks Cave levels cleared and the stars you've earned on each.
The Cave has new music: two calm cave pieces one after the other while you set up, and moodier strings for the whole fight.
The Cave crew is now Sword, Shield and Bow. Most baddies walk the paths, but some pop out of the ground and head straight for the Crystal Heart, including bats and hopping moles.
The Shroom Crew bar shows all three kinds at once without scrolling; tap one to pick it.
Farm sounds like rain and crickets go quiet while you're in the Cave.
The Cave's sweep now has a matching whoosh going in and coming out.
You can now place one of each Shroom Crew type.
On Cave Levels 2 to 6 you recruit each crew type for free, so you learn how recruiting works before it costs coins.
Going into the Cave sweeps the screen in purple, and coming back sweeps in your season's colours.
Clearing a Cave level now earns 1 to 5 stars for speed and keeping the Crystal Heart lit; five is a diamond, and your best for each level is saved.
The Cave's top-right card shows your level and skill points; tap it to pick any level you've reached.
New Shroom Crew skins in the skin store: buy one and put it on any crew type from its info card.
Setting Shroom Crew down, picking them up, taking them off, buying a stat and resetting stats have their own soft Cave sounds, and recruiting plays the happy harvest ding.
The Crystal Heart, Magic burst, Bow shot, Start and surge-over sounds are smoother, warmer magic now.
Your Cave sword has a new, sharper-looking icon held at an angle.
Fixed odd striped blocks appearing above baddies when they were hit.
Cave combat sounds are soft thuds and warm magic now.
The Crystal Heart's health now shows as a bar right above it during a fight.
Shroom Crew stats show their level as a row of glowing purple pips instead of a number.
The Cave panel no longer shows a crew count while you set up; the badges on the crew bar show it.
The cave entrance now glows softly purple, with the odd sparkle drifting out.
Replaying a Cave level starts with an empty field so you can place your crew fresh.

Cave Level 1 is just you and your sword; Shroom Crew join one at a time from Level 2 (Sword, Shield, Bow, Slow, Magic), free through Level 6. From Level 7 you recruit Shield, Bow, Slow and Magic crew once per level; then place up to 2 of each free. Swords are always free.
Shield crew now stand right on the path to hold back walking baddies; once the shield breaks they fight on with a dagger.
Cave paths now always reach the Crystal Heart from its left, right or front, never from behind it.
Shroom Crew are free to place on Cave Levels 1 to 5; they start costing coins from Cave Level 6.
Place Shroom Crew by dragging them onto the cave floor; tapping the floor now shows you how.
The Cave now has sound effects for swords, crew attacks, baddies, the Heart and surges.
The first Cave levels are much gentler: fewer, slower baddies while you learn.
Hits and defeats in the Cave look right again.
After a Cave win the Shroom Crew start cheering at once and keep hopping while the clear card is up, then walk out.
The Cave shows 'Cave Level N', calls the crystal the Crystal Heart, and has an Exit button at the top left that checks before you abandon a round.
Cave levels no longer have day names or tag lines: each is just Cave Level N.

New: the Cave. Tap the boulder cave in the top-right corner of the woods to defend the Crystal Heart from baddies, starting on the newest level each time you go in. Baddies follow glowing crystal-dust paths from 2 to 10 entrances to the Heart in one stream that builds up, surges every 20 seconds (watch for the "Surge!" warning at the entrances), eases off for a breath and ends in a final rush, while bats and moths fly straight in. Set down up to 10 Shroom Crew beside the paths, at most 2 of each kind, with a small badge such as 1/2 on each kind in the crew bar showing how many are set down. Level 1 has only the Sword, and each level after unlocks one more kind (Shield, Bow, Slow Magic, then Attack Magic on Level 5). Each kind's name shows under its picture on the crew bar. Set crew down by tapping the floor, dragging from the crew button, or dragging a kind up from the bar; drag crew to move them for free, then swipe your sword at the baddies. Win a level for the first time to earn rare ores, which you collect into Storage, and 5 skill points, paid only the first time you clear a level and added at once, and work your way down through 100 levels, whose rooms grow bigger deeper down. You can clear up to 5 new levels each farm day; tries and losses don't count, and pressing Start on a new level once they are used up says so. The clear card shows your time and the light you kept, then a Rewards card listing every ore, diamond and skill point you won, with a purple Collect. Under it, Replay plays the level again for no rewards, and Next Level goes on (greyed until midnight once the day's new levels are used up). A replay's card skips the rewards, and your crew come back free. The deepest levels give Rough Diamonds, and the first clear of Level 100 a chance at a building skin. Shooed baddies leave nothing behind.

Falling petals, leaves and other farm effects no longer freeze after a visit to the Cave, and the farm's time now carries on while you are down there: crops grow, animals and the tractor keep working, and midnight still brings the day's new Cave levels back. The new day's card and any change of season wait until you leave the Cave.
New Settings › Graphics choice, Forest Border: Rounded (default), Square, or None for the old open look; the cave entrance stays.
Tool levels on the tool bar now read 'Lvl 1' in the top-right corner.

New: the Cave. Tap the boulder cave in the top-right corner of the woods to defend the Heart of the Mountain from baddies, starting on the newest level each time you go in. Baddies follow glowing crystal-dust paths from 2 to 10 entrances to the Heart in one stream that builds up, surges every 20 seconds (watch for the "Surge!" warning at the entrances), eases off for a breath and ends in a final rush, while bats and moths fly straight in. Set down up to 10 Shroom Crew of any kinds beside the paths: retries and replays of that level bring them back, standing where you left them. Drag crew to move them for free, then swipe your sword at the baddies. Win a level for the first time to earn rare ores, which you collect into Storage, and 5 skill points, paid only the first time you clear a level and added at once, and work your way down through 100 levels, whose rooms grow bigger deeper down. Under it, Replay plays the level again for no rewards, and Next Level goes on (greyed until midnight once the day's new levels are used up). A replay's card skips the rewards, and your crew come back free. The deepest levels give Rough Diamonds, and the first clear of Level 100 a chance at a building skin. Shooed baddies leave nothing behind.

Shroom Crew stats: each of the 5 crew kinds has Attack Speed, Attack Power and Special Power (Wide Sweep for Sword, armour and regrowing shields for Shield, range and Skewer for Ranged, a stronger, wider slow for Slow Magic, a wider burst with a burning patch for Attack Magic), which you see and upgrade with skill points (1 per level) in the kind's "i" panel on the crew bar, each showing its level and what the next level gives. Upgrades belong to the kind, so they count on every level. Reset stats, in any kind's panel, resets all 5 kinds at once and gives every skill point back, for coins. Farms that had already cleared levels get the skill points those first clears would have paid.

New Cave baddies: the fast Glow Skitter from Level 12, the armoured Shell Beetle from Level 25 and the Lantern Moth, a flyer with a bubble that soaks up 3 hits, from Level 40. From Level 9 each level leans to Swarm, Stone or Wing baddies, shown on its title card. Sword and Shield crew can't reach flyers.

Cave prizes are collected into Storage. If Storage is too full when you tap Collect, a "Storage is full" message says how much room is needed, with Back, and Open Storage, which opens the Storage bar right there so you can sell or trash things and then collect.
Fish come back much faster to a lake with none left in it, and every kind of fish can now appear at any level; rarer fish just get likelier as you level up.
If Storage is too full for a cave prize, the prize card says how much room it needs and Make Room opens Storage right there, so you can sell or trash things and then collect.
The Cave now has its own music: a quiet cave hum, mysterious music while you get ready, battle music once the baddies come, and a victory fanfare when you win.
The cave room now sits at the bottom of stepped rock terraces that fade into the dark.

You can pan and zoom the camera in the Cave like on the farm: before Start, drag empty floor to pan (dragging a Shroom Crew moves it instead), and during a fight use two fingers, since one finger swings the sword.
The farm now sits in a clearing in dark oak woods that change with the seasons, growing darker further out until they fade to black.
The woods now meet the farm in rounded corners by default, so the clearing has soft corners.

Storage now opens in the tool bar instead of a menu: pick Storage on the tool button and the bar fills with what you have stored, each with how many (such as ×24), in a walnut-tinted bar. The item you pick shows on the tool button (food, decorations, fences, fertilizer, butterflies and fish still work on the farm as before), and the bar's "i" opens its card with Sell 1 and Sell All, or Trash for logs and stones; a fish's card also lists each fish to sell or rename. Tiles above the bar show how full Storage is and how many Trunks, Sheds and Silos you have placed (red when full, a padlock while locked), and tapping a building's tile opens its menu. The tool bars are a little slimmer, with thin lines between their items, and the tutorial's selling step now points you through the new bar.

Information panels no longer talk about upgrades: a locked item's stats no longer repeat the level on its lock, an animal home's Holds shows only what it holds now, and a tool no longer lists its upgrade levels. What an upgrade gives is shown on the Upgrade button and in the upgrade menu.
The camera now stays exactly on the animal it follows, with no lag or drift behind it as it walks.

The tutorial now works with the new tool bar: its finger points at the item you need on the bar (Wheat, the Scythe, the Axe, Farmland, Carrot, the Pet House and so on), never at the one already in the outline, the bar turns back to that item if you scroll it away or leave a locked item in the outline, Sell and Store are reached through the bar's "i" button, and picking Build with the Pet House in the outline counts as choosing it. The Carrot step now says "Switch to Carrot", as the bar names it. After you choose Store, and later Sell, it has you close the panel before moving on, and any step on the farm points at the panel's x while it is still open.
The tool bar now stops at the ends of its list.

The tool bar now scrolls freely under your finger and, when you let go, coasts on like any scrolling list, as far as your flick sends it, slowing to stop exactly on an item, which it then picks up; touching it while it coasts stops it there.

Items on the tool bar that have a limit now show how many you have placed out of how many are allowed, such as 0/5, as a tiny number at the bottom right of their picture, and the Scythe, Axe, Pickaxe, Bucket and Fishing Rod show their level there in the same style. Locked items show no count.
Fall's grass is a deeper tan-green.
Item pages and the Properties card now show how many are placed or planted (and farmland's unlocked tiles) as rows in the stats list, after the other numbers, instead of in boxes of their own.

New tool bar: picking a tool from the tool button now opens a bar of its items beside the button, three at a time in roomy cells whose names shrink slightly rather than cut off (crops go by the crop alone: Wheat, Carrot, Potato), the third fading out as it runs in behind the button at the bar's end, which stays open while you farm. The item in the green outline at the bar's left end is the one you hold; swipe the bar (it glides and settles on an item) or tap an item to bring it there, and the bar loops round endlessly. Items you haven't unlocked yet stay on the bar, greyed out with a padlock in the corner: you can look at them, but using one on the farm just says the level it unlocks at. The first time you open a tool on a farm it starts on the middle item it has unlocked, and after that on your last choice, which each farm keeps for itself. The green "i" button at the bar's right end opens a card about the item in the outline with everything its page said (what it is for, the level it unlocks at, what it takes, its numbers, how many are placed) and its settings (Sell or Store, a tree's size and color, water depth, a path's look and the like), which replace the dropdowns that sat beside the button, so the Open Tool Menu on Select setting is gone. Tapping the tool button again brings back the tools.

In Fall, small fallen leaves now lie on the grass: orange, red and gold ones over most of it, and a few more round each oak and birch in its own colours (gold under birches, browns and reds under brown oaks); pines drop none. A tree planted in Fall lets its leaves go from low in its crown, two or three at a time, and each drifts gently down, behind or in front of the tree, to where it lies; they fade away one by one over half a minute when it goes. Once all its leaves are down, each tree rests a few minutes, then its old leaves slowly fade away one by one as new ones drift down from its crown to fresh spots, every tree at its own pace, so a few are always dropping leaves wherever you look.
Tapping Play on the farm list now plays a button click, and the season whoosh and chime is now heard as the farm is revealed (it was being held silent until just after).

The music no longer switches songs partway through opening the game: with "Open my last farm automatically" on, it waits until it knows your farm, then fades in that farm's music, and the farm list's music fades in and then cross-fades once into the farm you open.

The Clouds switch in Settings › Graphics is now a "Hide Clouds Beyond" slider just under the grid lines one: clouds fade out as you zoom out past the chosen zoom, all the way left hides them always (what off was) and all the way right never hides them (what on was, and the default).

Dirt Path is now free, and Dirt Path and Brick Path are each one choice in the Terrain tool, with its look picked in its Properties card: Dark, Medium or Light for Dirt Path (Dark to start), Straight or Herringbone for Brick Path. Each remembers the look you last picked, and paths you already laid keep theirs. Brick, Cobblestone and Wood Plank Path stay $2 a tile.
Quests about planting trees now say they can be trees from Decorations or Crops.

The season's name, as a season changes and as a farm opens, now has a soft shadow and edge in a deep shade of the season's color, set a little out from the letters, so it stands out over snow and bright grass, with a slightly wider glow; its icon gets its own crisp shadow and outline too, and the line under it sits on a small pill tinted with the season's color and just says the day, such as "Day 29", without "a new season".

The launch screen is tidier: the carrot and name settle in the top third, your farms scroll below them, and "Open my last farm automatically", a New Game button and the iCloud button sit in their own strip at the bottom. Opening a farm plays the season whoosh and chime, and shows its season and day (turn it off with Show season on load in Settings › Graphics).
The Name your farm form sits lower under the logo, with its heading left-aligned like the options below it.
Each farm on the launch screen now has a Play button beside its three dots, so it is clear how to open it (tapping the card still works).

Chimney smoke is new: every 1.2 seconds a puff leaves the middle of the chimney's opening as a loose bunch of little puffs that merge into one soft, lumpy grey puff as it rises, drifts with the wind and fades. Every puff is a little different, the opening fills with a wisp of smoke as each one leaves, and the old plume and curls are gone. It is still darker in Winter, thinner in the rain, warm at the chimney at night and still with Reduce Motion.

The game now opens on a new launch screen: the carrot and "Stock Farmer" over a soft glow, then your farms slide in below as the main menu, each card showing its level, money and when you last played (play time and device are in Properties). Tap a farm and the season's sweep dissolves the screen away into your farm (a new farm also shows its season's title), or tick "Open my last farm automatically" (also in Settings › Gameplay) to go straight into your last farm as before.

Summer's grass now has little grass tufts scattered over it, the way Spring has its wildflowers: a mix of young shoots and taller clumps. They grow only on bare grass, so farmland, paths, water and anything you place hide them, and they come back when it goes.
Sell now comes first and Store second wherever you choose what the Scythe and Bucket do with what they gather (tool bar and item screens).

Market Stand quests now name the exact item: Cow Milk, Goat Milk, Chicken Egg and Sheep Wool. In Perfection, Snow is done as soon as you have seen Winter, since snow now falls all day; saves that already saw Winter count it done.

Tapping an entry in Progress now also says how often it turns up, with real odds for every fish at your level, chicks, baby animals, rocks, ore veins, wild trees, butterflies, fireflies, rain, snow, seasons and the tool levels that sometimes gather two.
New farms now start in Spring unless you pick another Starting Season.
A new farm's ponds now always start with an Uncommon fish as well as the Rare one; the rest are still Common.
A new farm now opens with its season sweeping in and its title rising, and the tutorial starts once the title has gone.
On Spring, Summer and Fall nights a coqui frog now calls its soft two-note "co-quí" among the crickets every so often, from 20 seconds to 3 minutes apart, following the Ambience volume.
Fixed the music sometimes starting a song twice when you start a new farm or switch farms: the farm's season theme now starts once, as the farm opens, and only one song ever plays at a time.
The change of season, and a farm opening from the menu, now sound only the soft whoosh of wind, without the little rising chime.

Cloth from Cotton now sells for $392 instead of $150, so turning Cotton into Cloth at the Tailor Table finally earns more than selling the Cotton. Wool now makes its own Wool Cloth, a cream-coloured good worth $135, which pays 1.5 times the Wool.
Each time a season begins, the music opens with that season's theme song, the first song in its song list (or the first one that is on), and then plays on as usual.

New Night Brightness slider in Settings → Graphics lightens the night if it looks too dark on your screen. It starts at the usual night, and all the way right makes the night half as dark, keeping its colour and the glow of the lights.

The Firefly Lantern and Cherry Blossom skins now take a small part of the memory they did, so a farm full of them runs lighter. They look the same, with their petals and fireflies moving a little faster.

Twelve new animated skins for every building and the Trunk, in every season. Epic: Haunted, Honeybee, Crystal Geode, Neon Sign, Lily Frog, Ghost Flame and Meteor Shower. Legendary: Galaxy Swirl, Prismatic, Pixie Dust, Duck Parade and Molten Chrome. Haunted, Crystal Geode, Neon Sign, Ghost Flame, Meteor Shower, Galaxy Swirl and Pixie Dust also glow at night.

Every building menu and the Trunk now has a Move button, which closes the menu and picks the building up to move, the same as holding a finger on it. On the Market Stand it sits beside Sell, and on the House at the bottom of the Stock Market tab.

New setting in Settings → Sound: Play in Background, off unless you turn it on. With it on, the game keeps playing when you lock your phone or switch apps: the music, with the song, its cover and previous, play or pause and next on the lock screen and in Control Center, and the farm's rain, crickets, thunder and birds as they were when you left. Pick Music Only under it to keep just the music. Taps, sales and other action sounds stay quiet, the farm's clock still waits for you, and coming back carries on where the sound was. Pausing on the lock screen or taking out headphones quiets everything, and the silent switch doesn't mute the game while this is on.
The plain Trunk now opens in the same wood colours it has when closed, instead of turning a paler wood as the lid lifts.
The skin unlock celebration now ends with Equip, which puts the new skin on the building you bought it from, and Later, which leaves it for the preview.
Light colour skins such as Chalk White no longer leave stray black dots and dashes on the House and upgraded House roofs or on the Luxury Barn's walls.
With an animal's or fish's menu open, tapping another animal or fish now switches the menu to it at the same small size, instead of the menu filling the screen.
The skin unlock celebration now uses the same big rounded lettering as the season-change title.

Tapping a Trunk now opens its lid and then a menu like the buildings', with an Info tab (how full storage is, Sell and its facts) and a Skins tab. The Trunk has skins like the buildings: the 16 colours, plus Paw Prints, Starry Night, Firefly Lantern, Cherry Blossom, Gold Leaf, Ember and Hoarfrost, bought once for every Trunk and equipped on each one, and its lid opens in the skin's colours, in Winter too with the snow on the lid, stays open while its menu is up and closes again when the menu does.
The skin unlock celebration now shows the skin you bought from the start, instead of the original look changing into it.
The Shed now unlocks at level 6, costs 35 logs and is listed above the Market Stand, which unlocks at level 7 and costs 38 logs.
An animal home's Info tab now says what it spawns and makes in one line, such as "Spawns a Rabbit every 4 min which produces fertilizer", instead of separate lines for the new baby and what it gives.
The Upgrade dialog now shows what improves as the new value with a green gain, such as "Holds 7 (+3) Rabbits", instead of "4 → 7".
Petting a fish no longer sends a ring out across the water; the hearts and sound stay. A fish you have never caught now shows just ??? in its menu, without the "Never caught" line.

Each Trunk you set down now adds 25 slots to storage. It now costs $100, you can place at most 4, and it is in the Build list right after the Pet House instead of the Decorate list. The Storage menu lists it beside the Shed and Silo with how many you have placed, opening its page when tapped.
A new farm now lets you pick its Starting Season (Spring, Summer, Fall or Winter, Summer by default) under its name, and it begins on day 1 of that season.
A Pet House's Info tab now shows its pet's details above the buttons, with Sell last.
The loading bar on the launch screen now fills smoothly to almost full, waits there while your farm loads, then finishes the last bit once it is ready, instead of creeping along and jumping.

In the animal's menu, the progress bar under the countdown now fills for every animal that makes something, hens included, as well as for babies and chicks growing up; while the animal is Well Fed it turns purple with a purple pixel chevron hopping at its tip. Hens now count down to their exact next egg instead of saying "about", and lay just as often on average.

Skins are now bought and equipped in each building's own menu instead of the Market Stand: its Skins tab shows the original look, then a sideways row each of Common, Rare, Epic and Legendary skins, cheapest first, each showing its price until you own it, then a green check, and a green ring with an Equipped tag on the one it has on. Tap a skin to see it big in any season by day or night (Firefly Lantern starts at night), swipe left or right for the next or previous skin, then Buy it for every building of its kind or Equip it on that one building; after the purchase's celebration, Done brings you back to Equip it. Common skins are now marked in leaf green and Legendary in orange, and the Market Stand's tabs are now Quests, Supplies and Skins, its Skins tab holding only the stand's own skins, and tapping the House opens Stock Market and Skins tabs with your money at the top.

Every building's menu now opens on an Info tab beside Skins, with its name centred and your money at the top and a Close button at the bottom like the other menus (or swipe it down): a card with its picture, level or what it is doing and a live timer, one row of buttons for what you can do there (such as Choose Chick, Recipe, Start, Upgrade and Sell, or a slim Sell button when that is all there is), with room around it, and its facts as a short list. Upgrade opens a small window showing what the next level changes and what it costs, or the level you need to reach first. The tabs of the building menus, the Market Stand and the House now all use the same lettering, and so do the headings inside them.
In every menu with a Close button at the bottom, such as Storage, Progress, the House and the buildings, the list now ends above Close instead of scrolling behind it.
Thunder rolls about 20% more often during rain, and one gentle, soft rumble now sounds just before each day's rain begins.
Gunmetal is now a Rare building skin instead of Common, so it costs 12.5 times the building's price (at least $2,500) rather than 5 times. Skins you already bought stay yours.
Tar Black is now a Rare building skin too, priced the same way as Gunmetal. Skins you already bought stay yours.
The bird chirp no longer has the windy rumble of a bird flying past the microphone under it, so you hear only the chirps.

Building skins now cost half as much: Common 5 times the building's price, Rare 12.5 times, Epic 25 times and Legendary 50 times, with a least price of $1,250 to $7,500 by tier, and Gold Leaf is $500,000 on every building. Skins you already bought stay yours with no refund.

Taking a building down is now called Sell, since it gives money back, and each building's menu has a Sell row at the very bottom showing what you get back; the question says "Skins you've bought stay yours" when you own skins for that kind. Crops, fertilizer and anything that pays nothing back still say Destroy.
Chimney smoke now rises in front of its own house instead of behind it.
Rabbits that stop after a hop now sit down properly instead of staying frozen mid-hop.

At night, food dropped on the tile in front of a Chicken Coop, Pet House, Rabbit Hutch, barn or Stable no longer feeds an animal that has gone inside; animals indoors leave that tile free for planting, terrain and fertilizer.
Cloud shadows now stay visible in the rain and at night, just fainter: 60% of their daytime strength in rain, 75% at night and 45% on a rainy night.
Every tool's dropdown list now opens at its top instead of scrolled to the chosen row, and Fence colour shows its price like other prices, in red when you can't afford it.

The Market Stand has a new Shop tab that sells ore, gems, logs and stone for money: Copper Ore $100, Silver Ore $250, Gold Ore $450, Rough Ruby $700, Rough Sapphire $1,000, Logs and Stone $100 each. It sells at most 10 of each ore and 50 Logs and 50 Stone a day, and restocks every new day.

Buildings can now wear skins, bought at the Market Stand's new skins tab: 16 Common colours (such as Gunmetal, Harbour Navy, Buttercup and Oxblood) and seven animated skins, Paw Prints (Rare), Starry Night, Firefly Lantern and Cherry Blossom (Epic), Ember, Hoarfrost and Gold Leaf (Legendary), several of which glow at night. The Common colours cost 10 times the building's price, Rare 25 times, Epic 50 times and Legendary 100 times, with a least price of $2,500 to $15,000 by tier, and Gold Leaf is $1,000,000 on every building. A skin is bought once for every building of its kind once you have built one, previewed first in any season by day or night, and picked from the Skin list in the building's own menu. Buying one celebrates it full screen: the building pops into its new skin with a fanfare, a shockwave and confetti in the tier's colour, grander the rarer the skin, then Equip now wears it straight away or Later keeps it for the building's menu. The Market Stand's awning is now red and white, with its old yellow look sold as Classic Yellow, and a Luxury Barn you built in Blue, Grey or Yellow now wears Harbour Navy, Gunmetal or Buttercup, owned.

Buildings can now wear skins, bought at the Market Stand's new skins tab: 16 Common colours (such as Gunmetal, Harbour Navy, Buttercup and Oxblood) and seven animated skins, Paw Prints (Rare), Starry Night, Firefly Lantern and Cherry Blossom (Epic), Ember, Hoarfrost and Gold Leaf (Legendary), several of which glow at night. The Common colours cost 10 times the building's price, Rare 25 times, Epic 50 times and Legendary 100 times, with a least price of $2,500 to $15,000 by tier, and Gold Leaf is $1,000,000 on every building. A skin is bought once for every building of its kind once you have built one, previewed first in any season by day or night in a preview that stays at the top while you scroll the skins and changes as you tap each one, and picked from the Skin list in the building's own menu. The Market Stand's Quests, Shop and Skins switch is bigger, with an icon on each tab and a rainbow Skins label marked NEW until you first open it, and the Market Stand's description now says it has quests, a daily ore shop and skins. The Market Stand's awning is now red and white, with its old yellow look sold as Classic Yellow, and a Luxury Barn you built in Blue, Grey or Yellow now wears Harbour Navy, Gunmetal or Buttercup, owned.
The Terrain tool's list now always opens at its top, and Grass sits right below Farmland and shows Free like the other free ground.
The bird chirp sound no longer includes the loud wing-flapping thumps, so it is just the chirping.
Settings → About has a link to the new Stock Farmer Wiki, which explains how everything in the game works.

Every fish is now one of a kind. Each has its own weight, and its size and price follow it: a light fish sells for up to a fifth less than its rarity's price and a heavy one up to a fifth more (Common $10 to $14, Legendary $800 to $1,200). The first time you catch a fish it gets a number, like "King Salmon #5", which is its name until you give it one. The catch card is titled with just the fish's name, with no "You caught" and no number in it (the number sits small beside its weight, like "#5 · 31.0 lb · $311"), and shows its price and a gold "New!" for the first of a kind. Fish of a kind you have caught now show faintly in the pond as themselves; kinds you have never caught are still dark shadows. Tap a fish with anything but the Fishing Rod to open its menu, the fish outlined in a soft white glow like a tapped animal: see its weight and price, Pet it (even a fish of a kind you have not caught yet), Nudge it, give it a name (a named fish no longer swims off) or Release it for good. In Storage each kind of fish shows what they are worth together with no buttons of its own: tap the row to list every fish, newest catch first, each with Sell and Rename (let a fish go on water by picking it in the Decorate tool); a fish you let go keeps its number and name, and catching it again gives no XP. Fish already in Storage got numbers and weights.
The House now unlocks at level 10 (was 12), so the Stock Market opens sooner.

Every fish is now one of a kind. Each has its own weight, and its size and price follow it: a light fish sells for up to a fifth less than its rarity's price and a heavy one up to a fifth more (Common $10 to $14, Legendary $800 to $1,200). The first time you catch a fish it gets a number, like "King Salmon #5", which is its name until you give it one. The catch card is titled with just the fish's name, with no "You caught" and no number in it (the number sits small beside its weight, like "#5 · 31.0 lb · $311"), and shows its price and a gold "New!" for the first of a kind. Fish of a kind you have caught now show faintly in the pond as themselves; kinds you have never caught are still dark shadows. Tap a fish with anything but the Fishing Rod to open its menu: see its weight and price, Pet it (even a fish of a kind you have not caught yet), Nudge it, give it a name (a named fish no longer swims off) or Release it for good. In Storage each kind of fish shows what they are worth together with no buttons of its own: tap the row to list every fish, newest catch first, each with Sell and Rename (let a fish go on water by picking it in the Decorate tool); a fish you let go keeps its number and name, and catching it again gives no XP. Fish already in Storage got numbers and weights.

The album cover on Now Playing (Settings → Sound) now changes with the season of the music: each season has its own cover in the style of the season-change title, with its icon and name glowing in the season's color over the farm's hills, sky and weather (Spring petals, Summer sunlight, Fall leaves, Winter snow). When the season turns, the new cover fades in as the music crosses over.

When a chicken or farm animal eats one of your crops on its own, it is now fed just as if you had fed it by hand: five minutes Well Fed, making its milk, eggs, wool or fertilizer 25% faster, with the Feed countdown and boosted bar in its menu. An animal that is already Well Fed is full and leaves your crops alone. Crops eaten this way still don't count toward feeding quests.

Eggs are now picked up like crops, never mistaken for the hen: tapping an egg lying beside a hen goes to the egg, not her menu (tap the hen herself for that). Only the Bucket collects it; tapping an egg with any other tool, or holding a finger on it, says "Use the Bucket from the Harvest tool to collect eggs". Nothing can be planted, built, fertilized or set down on top of an egg (dragging seeds or terrain across one just skips its tile), and trees and rocks no longer grow over one.
The song "Sheep" has been taken out of Spring's music.

Each season in the song list (Settings → Sound, the list button on Now Playing) now has a shuffle button, off to begin with. With it on, that season's music starts on a random song every time the season begins, whether you open the game into it or the season changes, then plays its songs in a random order, a fresh one each time round. Songs you have unchecked stay out, and you can still tap a song to play it. Reset to Default turns shuffle off.

Six soft, slightly see-through pixel clouds now drift slowly and smoothly across the farm with the wind, each casting a soft shadow on the ground a couple of tiles away. They sit over the farm itself, moving with the ground as you drag and zoom, and are already there when the farm opens. There are always six on the map: as one fades out over the far edge, a new one fades in on the side the wind blows from. They turn grey and hurry along in the rain (with no shadows), take on a cool blue-grey under white tops over Winter's snow so they stand out from it, and turn moonlit blue at night. They fade away when you zoom in any closer than the farm opens at, never get in the way of taps, and hold still with Reduce Motion. Turn them off with the new Clouds switch in Settings → Graphics.

Tapping an animal now opens a small menu that fits what it shows, with the farm still in view and the animal ringed in a soft white glow that follows it as it walks. Under its name, each kind of animal has its own little personality line, such as "Makes milk, can't read" for a cow or "Just a little baby" for every baby. Below that, animals that grow up or make something have a line saying what they are up to, such as "Next milk in 2m 40s" or "Grows up in 12m 40s", with a blue bar; once its milk, egg or wool is waiting the line turns green and says which tool collects it, such as "Milk waiting · use the Bucket". Below are Feed, Pet and Nudge. Feed shows Wheat and lights up green when the animal is hungry and you have food: tap it to pick a food from your storage, favorite first. While the animal is Well Fed, Feed counts down the rest of its meal and the bar turns purple with little arrows racing along it; with no food stored it says "No Food". Cats, dogs, roosters and grown ducks show only their personality line, and cats, dogs and grown ducks have no Feed in the menu, but you can still drop food on them. Collect what animals give with the Harvest tool on the farm. A button at the bottom sells ducks and ducklings for $25 or releases any other animal, and asks first. You can now release your pet too: its Pet House stays empty until you choose a new pet in the house's menu.

Thunder now rolls through every rain shower, loud enough to hear clearly over the rain, in Spring, Summer and Fall, about every minute, in four different rolls from near to far, never the same one twice in a row. Lightning is rare: only about one shower in ten brings a soft flash across the farm now and then (not with Reduce Motion). Winter snow stays quiet. Thunder follows the Ambience volume and fades away when the rain stops.
The Shed now costs $500 (was $2,500) and the Silo $1,500 (was $7,000), so more storage is easy to add as your farm grows.

The loading page now checks for a newer version of the game just before syncing with iCloud, so an update message is ready sooner. It waits at most a second and a half and says "Checking for update…" when it takes a moment; offline or on a slow connection, the farm opens as usual and the check finishes in the background.

Each season's music now plays in a chosen order, opening gently, mixing calmer and livelier songs and ending on its calmest, instead of in alphabetical order. A new list button in the top right of the Now Playing card (Settings → Sound) shows every season's songs in the order they play, with the song playing highlighted. Uncheck a song to leave it out of its season (each season keeps at least one), tap a song of the season playing to play it, and tap Rearrange to drag songs into a new order or into another season. Reset to Default puts every song back. Your choices are kept on this device.

The midnight wave now brings more of what your farm is missing for your level: with plenty of trees and rocks it brings Copper Veins instead, a farm short of trees or rocks gets more of them, and Silver, Gold, Ruby and Sapphire Veins turn up more often the closer you get to the level you can smelt or cut them.
Settings → About has a new Credits page naming who made the game's art, music and sounds: each work with its author and licence, and a tap on its title opens its page in Safari.

When a newer version of the game is ready (a new TestFlight build, or a new version on the App Store), a message says so once your farm has opened, with Update and Ignore. Update takes you to TestFlight or the App Store; after Ignore, that version never asks again, and a yellow pulsing "!" sits between your money and your Level until you update. Tap it to see the message again. With Reduce Motion it stays still.

Every chicken and farm animal's favorite food is now Wheat, and every cat and dog's is Salmon, in place of a different favorite crop for each kind. Feeding quests now read "Hand-feed 10 favorite foods to animals from the Sheep Barn" and count Wheat (or Salmon); quests you already have keep their progress. The animal menu no longer has a favorite line.

Every building's page in the Build menu now has a short line under its picture saying what it does, such as "Spawns cows that provide milk for recipes" or "Offers optional quests for extra XP". The Shed and Silo say how many storage slots they add (50 and 150), and the Pet House reads "A home for your furry friend".
Every building's page in the Build menu now has a short line under its picture saying what it does, such as "Spawns cows that provide milk for recipes" or "Offers optional quests for extra XP".

Four new songs join Summer's music: Farm Music by migfus20, Another August by The Cynic Project (cynicmusic.com / pixelsphere.org), Costal Town by Hitctrl and Sunset Plains by Yoiyami (all from OpenGameArt.org).
Crickets now sing softly under the music on Spring, Summer and Fall nights, rising as it gets dark and fading away at dawn; Winter nights stay quiet under the snow. They follow the Ambience volume.

The Shed and Silo pictures under the Storage bar are now in full colour as soon as you unlock them, built or not, with a small count on the corner of how many you have out of the most you can build, like "0/4" or "2/4" (gold once you have them all). A picture stays grey with no count until you reach its level, and tapping one still opens it in the Build menu.

A meal fed by hand now makes an animal give its milk, goat milk, wool, fertilizer or eggs 25% faster for its five minutes, instead of twice as fast, and its menu shows the quicker time while it is Well Fed. An animal still holds only one thing at a time: once it is ready it waits for you to collect it, fed or not, and makes no start on the next one until you do. Babies, ducklings and chicks included, also grow up 25% faster while fed, and a fed pet is 25% more likely to ripen the crop it stands on, instead of twice.

Seasons now change at 6 AM, once it is fully light, on the day they are due, instead of at midnight. Crops, weather, music and the ground all change with it, and each season still lasts 7 days. If you were away past 6 AM on that day, the change plays when you come back; picking a season on the Time sheet still changes it straight away.

When a new season sweeps in, its own weather is already there behind the gust, as if through a window: Winter's snow is falling and Fall's leaves or Spring's petals are in the air, while the old season's weather keeps falling and blowing on the side the gust hasn't reached yet. Nothing freezes while it sweeps: animals, water, smoke, lights, fireflies, trees and everything you do keep moving on both sides, each tree, building and crop turning into its new look as the gust passes over it. The gust carries fewer snowflakes of its own now that Winter's snow shows through.

Every animal now eats any food you feed it by hand: pets, chickens (roosters and chicks too) and every farm animal, ducks included, take any crop, any fruit basket from your fruit trees, any fish, eggs, milk, flour, bread, cheese and anything made from them, such as juice, preserves, pie, soup and pickles. Pick a food in Storage or the Decorate tool's list and drag it onto an animal. Every meal gives the same five-minute boost as before; only an animal's favorite food counts toward feeding quests.

A new season now sweeps across the farm in a gust from top left to bottom right, with a glittering edge in the season's colors and petals, sun motes, leaves or snow trailing behind, while you keep playing. The season's name rises into focus from below once the gust has passed it, lingers a few moments and sinks away; the music fades into the new season's and a soft whoosh and chime plays. It waits until the level-up and day summary are closed, plays after the farm loads if the season changed while the game was closed, and also plays when you pick a season on the Time sheet. With Reduce Motion the new season simply fades in. This replaces the full-screen splash and "is here" message.
When you move a building, decoration or tree, the arrows round it are now chunky pixel chevrons that match the farm's art and hop gently outward; the one you drag turns gold.
When you chop a tree or break a rock or ore vein, its count and bar now show just above your finger, so your finger no longer hides how close it is to coming down.
Hide Grid Lines Beyond in Settings → Graphics now starts at 2.0×, so grid lines fade away sooner as you zoom out; Reset to Defaults sets it there too. A zoom you already picked is kept.
Tapping an animal that already has a name now offers Rename instead of Name, and its naming box says "Rename it".

Seasons now last 7 days each, instead of 14, going Spring, Summer, Fall, Winter and round again. A season you pick on the Time sheet also lasts 7 days from that day. A farm you already have keeps the season it is in when you open it, and its next change comes within 7 days.

In the tutorial, the steps that find and gather from a tree, rock, ore vein or fish now pick one and keep pointing at that same one, glowing gold, until the step is done, instead of jumping to whichever is nearest as you look around; another is picked only if it disappears.
The tutorial no longer puts red dots on the buttons and rows it points at; they swell with a gold glow instead.
In the tutorial, "Pinch to zoom in on the tree" (or rock, ore vein or fish) now shows two fingers spreading apart over it, the opposite of the zoom-out step's pinch.
The tutorial now only points you at small trees, small rocks and Copper Veins to chop and mine, even when a bigger tree or rock is closer. If none are left, small ones turn up near your field.
Chimney smoke is a little thicker where it leaves the chimney, so it shows against any roof or ground, and still fades out as it rises.
Lanterns come in a new Leaf green colour, with green glass and a soft green light at night.

At night a Lantern's lit glass, the buildings' lit windows and the Christmas lights are now hidden behind anything standing in front of them, such as a rock, tree or building, instead of shining through it; only their soft glow still spreads over everything.
Tapping a hen now says about how long until her next egg, or that her egg is ready; farm animals say "Milk in 2 min" or "Milk ready" in the same way.
The Storage menu shows a Shed and a Silo under its fill bar in place of the text, greyed until you have one; tap either to see its page from the Build menu.
The Bucket now starts on Sell on a new farm, like the Scythe, so eggs, milk, wool and fruit sell the moment you gather them; switch either to Store whenever you like.
When a farm can't be opened, the message now says to retry or restore a backup, which the Load Game menu's farm options offer.

Settings → Timelapse has a Picture size menu, from Smallest (1024 × 1024) to Largest (4096 × 4096), showing about how much room each picture and each day takes; it sets the size of both timelapse screenshots and Screenshot Farm photos, which start at Medium (2048 × 2048).
Settings → Timelapse can take up to three screenshots a day: add, change or remove capture times, and a day's screenshots play in time order.
Timelapse screenshots, and the video made from them, no longer show tile grid lines.

Moving a building, tree, fruit tree or decoration has a Nudge button that opens a Nudge pad, like the Lantern's, under the Move menu, shifting just its picture a quarter of a tile toward any side or corner; the picture stays nudged when a fruit tree is picked, a pet hurries a plant along or a wild tree grows.
While a timelapse plays or is paused, pinch to zoom in on the farm and drag to look around; double-tap to zoom in on a spot or back out.

Screenshot Farm pictures and timelapse screenshots now show the farm in the middle with the same margin of empty space on every side, so a Silo, barn, House or tall tree on the farm's edge is no longer cut off.

Settings → Timelapse has Export Video: it turns your farm's daily screenshots into a short video, each day a second (quicker for long timelapses), and Share Video then sends it to Photos, Messages or any other app.

Moving something gives it a soft glow round its shape, white where it fits and red where it can't go, and a gold handle on each side; tap a handle to step one tile, or drag a handle or the thing itself to move it any way a tile at a time.

The Move menu is now a small glass tag hanging under the thing being placed or moved (above it near the bottom of the screen), with its picture and name, whether it fits or why not, a bin for something already standing, and Nudge, Place and Cancel; Place is greyed out while it can't go there, and the bin asks right in the tag.
Both Houses' brick chimneys now meet the roof without a dark seam line, in every season.

Settings → Sound has a new Now Playing card: an album cover with the song's name and artist, previous, play/pause and next buttons, and the music volume slider, replacing the old Music slider and song line.

Animals no longer get hungry: they give their eggs, milk, wool and fertilizer at their usual pace without needing to eat, and the hungry picture over their heads is gone. Instead grown chickens and farm animals are now and then pests: one that wanders onto a crop may eat it, at most one crop a day each; fence your fields to keep them out. Feeding favorites by hand still gives a short boost.
Hens now lay their eggs on the ground wherever they happen to be walking, instead of carrying them over their heads; collect them with the Bucket where they lie.

Whenever a farm becomes Spring or Fall, whether it loads, you open another farm, pick a season, the season turns on its own or you return to the app, the first petals or leaves now cross the screen straight away, instead of a minute later.
Spring's grass has 15% more wildflowers.
The Axe now chops a tree wherever you tap or swipe on its picture, its leaves included, not only on the tile under its trunk.
The first-level House no longer hangs a second strand of Christmas lights along the beam above its door, in any season.

The House's chimney now smokes, at both levels: a soft, puffy plume that drifts with the wind, with a soft curl of smoke rising smoothly straight up about a second after the last one fades, turning left and right by turns. The Stone Oven's flue smokes the same way, smaller, while it bakes. The smoke is a darker grey in Winter so it shows on the snow, thinner in the rain, glows faintly warm at the chimney at night, and stands still with Reduce Motion.

New Lantern at the top of the Decorate menu ($25, 4 Logs and 2 Copper Ore): a small wooden lantern on one tile that casts a soft, cosy wash of coloured light all round it at night over the ground, buildings, trees and crops nearby, flickering softly like the building windows (steady with Reduce Motion). Tap it to pick its color (Candle yellow, Warm amber, Soft white, Pale blue or Rose; its glass is colored to match), its Brightness (Low, Medium or High), its Range (Short, Medium or Long), its Power (Auto at night and in rain, Always on or Always off) and an Effect (Flicker or Steady) and a nudge to any of nine spots within its tile. A lantern put away with the Axe keeps its settings.

A decoration, tree, crop, rock or animal standing on the same bottom row as a building is now drawn on top of the building instead of behind it, while a fence there stays behind it (the building's Christmas lights stay with the building).

Every tree and Christmas Tree, at every size, now stands on just the one tile under its trunk, drawn centred on it, with its leaves spreading over the tiles around, which stay free for animals, paths and anything else. Trees on your farm move onto the tile under their trunk.

Planting or moving a tree can no longer replace another tree by accident: a tree, decoration, building or path can't go on the tile a tree or Christmas Tree stands on, and a farm that already had two trees on one spot keeps one and pays back any of yours it removes.

Bigger trees give far more logs: Small trees 3, Medium 7, Big 15 and Huge 30, so a new farm's forest holds enough to build everything once. A first Axe takes one swing per log, so big trees take many swings; upgraded Axes still halve that and then fell any tree in one.

New farms start with fewer plain rocks and many more ore veins, including a Ruby and two Sapphire veins, and together they hold enough stone and ore to build every building and decoration once. Rocks and veins now give twice as much or more (Small, Medium and Big rocks 5, 10 and 15 stones; Copper veins 12 ore, gems 6), and a first Pickaxe takes one swing for each stone or ore it gives.
The midnight wave glows brighter in every season: each of its pixels now has its own soft halo in its own color, so the pixels stand out clearly, even on Winter's snow.

Night window lights are softer and more natural in every season: the House (door window included), Shed, Rabbit Hutch, Sheep, Goat and Pig Barns and the Luxury Barns now glow from a lamp inside with the frames and bars showing, and the Stone Oven's fire glows up from its hearth inside the arch, still flickering. Every building's night light, windows and doorways alike, now pulses gently like the Chicken Coop's, each building in its own time so the farm never pulses together (they stay steady with Reduce Motion).
Animals and pets can now walk behind trees and Christmas Trees, wandering into the tiles under the leaves and disappearing behind them; only the row a tree stands on still blocks them.

The seasons' music is reshuffled: Spring gains Gymnopédie No.1 and loses Path To Lake Land and Synthwave 15k, Summer gains Evening Harmony, Fall now opens with Memories Of A Lost Autumn and gains Path To Lake Land, and Winter now opens with Winter Is Coming and gains Synthwave 15k, Wanderer's Tale, No More Magic and The Fallen. Minuet, Pineapple Under The Sea, Whispering Woods and Strange Worlds are gone from the game.
The farm can now be dragged much further at any zoom, until most of it is off screen; a strip of it always stays in view so you can drag it back.

Christmas lights in Winter: colored string lights hang along the roof edges of the Houses, Barns, Luxury Barns, Stable, Silo, Market Stands, Shed, Rabbit Hutch, Chicken Coop and Pet House, and at night and in the rain their bulbs glow like the Christmas Tree's, and now and then a few bulbs at a time, never neighbors together, swell with a soft glow of their color and settle back, so the string gently twinkles without ever blinking (with Reduce Motion they stay solid). Settings > Graphics > Christmas Lights holds three choices: Power (Always On, which also glows softly by day and is how new players start, Always Off, which keeps the strands but no glow, or Auto, which glows at night and in rain), Pattern (Twinkling or Solid) and All Year (Yes shows them in every season, No only in Winter). Your earlier Solid/Twinkling and Always show choices carry over.
Spring now has flower petals on the wind: now and then a gust carries a few small pink, white and pale yellow petals tumbling across the farm, just like Fall's leaves.

New Settings > Graphics > Weather effects switch, on to start with: turn it off to hide the falling rain and snow and the darker tint under them, the Fall leaves, the Spring petals and the curls of wind. The weather itself carries on, so the animals still go in when it pours and the rain is still heard.

Snow now falls all through Winter, day and night: lighter most of the time and heavier in the 2 PM to 5 PM storm. The animals still only go in, and windows only light up for the weather, during those hours. Rain and snow also keep falling when the wind changes direction, instead of stopping partway.

Rocks, ore veins and the small standing decorations (Pumpkins, Decorative Watermelon, Small Hay Pile, Scarecrow, Crop and Wooden Signs, Milk Cans, Milk Baskets, Wooden Stool, Empty Basket, Dressmaker Display, Trunk, Pet Bowl and Weathercock) now stand up off the ground: the base of each, where it really meets the ground (a rock's foot rather than the shadow under it, a pumpkin's round bottom, a sign's or scarecrow's post), sits on the middle of its tile and the rest rises over the tile behind it, the way trees do, drawn in front of whatever stands there. Each still takes up only its own tile, which is where it is tapped, mined or moved, and butterflies land on the thing itself.

Three new paths in the Terrain tool, Wood Plank Path, Brick Path and Herringbone Brick Path, each $2 a tile from the start: square, a step below the grass like every path, with the same soft shadow under the grass, and clear of snow in Winter.
Paths stay clear of snow in Winter: the dirt paths, in every shade, and the stone path look just as they do in Summer, with no frost.

New decoration: the Christmas Tree, a green pine hung with colored string lights and a star, in Small, Medium, Big and Huge, for $80, 8 logs and a Copper Ore. Like a planted pine it takes up only the row it stands on, one tile for Small and two for the others, and rises over the tiles behind it, which stay free. It wears snow in Winter, and at night and in the rain its bulbs and star light up with a soft colored glow, a few of its bulbs at a time swelling with a soft glow while the star shines steadily.

About half the trees on the farm, of every kind and size, and the Christmas Trees, are now drawn facing the other way, so the woods look less uniform. Each tree always faces the same way. Trees are now tapped, chopped and picked up only on the row they stand on, and the outline when planting or moving one shows just that row.
Lit windows at night and in the rain now sit exactly on each building's windows in every season, including the redrawn Fall and Winter Houses, the grey Luxury Barn in Fall and the Shed in Fall.

Buildings with no windows now glow from their doorway at night and in the rain, in every season: the Silo shed's door has four glass panes that light up amber, the Stable's stalls glow with soft lamplight on their wood, and the Stone Oven's mouth glows the orange of the old door torch. The Chicken Coop's and Pet House's doorways glow amber, strongest at the top of the opening and fading to a faint glow at the floor, with no light on the step.
